📡 The Mirror Draft is not for strangers. Face what hunts you now — stand on the grid with the Final Draft, more than once, more than one kind.
It turns its face toward you. The face is a mirror. You see yourself — tired, dirty, afraid. It starts walking. Not running. Walking. That's worse.
(Don't meet its gaze — if it locks eyes, you FREEZE. Break line of sight, keep moving sideways. It charges in a straight line.)
The village is rattled. Everyone's jumpy — eyes on the treeline.

Venison, technically. The mirror-face is not edible. Do not eat the mirror. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.

◈ THE TABLE — it is not a table. It's a ring of pale light, and around it, things with too many angles to be faces. Above it all — the audience. Trillions of eyes, and every one of them knows your name. The System speaks, and for once it isn't performing: "HUMANITY PRESENTS ITS CASE."

◈ THE AUDIT — the System reads your run back to you, and the galaxy listens. A lesser seat — regional standing, waves 1–3 faced (13/9/3), 6 contests survived, 4 crises weathered. The table does not rise. It prices.
The table notes 1 ascension from one village — its terms improve accordingly. Nobody has ever seen that before.

◈ ABILITY — War-table: You read the table's fear the way you read weather. The Nielsen flinches first — you saw it.
◈ THE FEARED — "Look what eating built." The footage plays unasked — the deer, the fire, the ones who came for you and didn't come back. Nobody at the table is comfortable. That is the point.
The table has read your ledger. The food truth was shared. The light road is open.
The deer. The cleanest kill. The table goes very still. Behind you, your own people go still too — a different stillness.
You let them see it. All of it. The table recalculates. The fire back home burns a little lower.
You spend it — the shield, not the sword. The small envoy stares. Your people stand a little straighter. Protective terror: the table writes it down and doesn't understand it, which is the point.

The most frightening thing you ever did. The table doesn't know what to do with mercy from a predator. Neither do you, quite. But the audience weeps, and the galaxy learns that the feared one chose gentleness — and that choice echoes longer than any threat. The terror stays, pledged now: a shield ov
The terms held — the table had priced the village, ascension and all, and the village paid in full.
Not won yet — the table only waits on time. But the ending is already written: the village endures, the table will sign, and the applause will be real, and you will have earned it.
◈ THE TABLE WAITS — "Ninety days. We do not price a life half-lived. Come back when the village has seen ninety dawns — the table will still be here."
